decisions.why: *anxiári* (ἀκηδιάσαι, to be weighed down, faint) is in the psalter only here and at 142:3b *anxiátus est … spíritus meus* (grep); *angustiar-se* is the plain word for it, and MS1932 has *estava angustiado*. *dum* is 'while / when'; *quando* is shorter than *enquanto* in a colon that is already long. The verb comes before its subject so that the colon can be split where the Latin antiphon splits it (*Dum anxiarétur * Cor meum, in petra exaltásti me*, Pent02-5.txt, found by grep): *Quando se angustiava * o meu coração, sobre uma rocha me exaltastes*. **v2:** the stylist found the inverted *se angustiava o meu coração* made the ear wait for the main verb in a long colon, and asked *enquanto meu coração se angustiava, sobre a rocha*. The order is taken (D2: order yields to the ear) — the clause now closes on its verb before the turn; *quando* (shorter), *o meu* (the article before possessives, rule 5) and *uma rocha* (= 26:6) are kept. Cost: the antiphon of Pent02-5 splits *Dum anxiarétur * Cor meum*; in Portuguese it would split *Quando o meu coração * se angustiava, …*, which still reads.

decisions.why: ἀπὸ προσώπου ἐχθροῦ: a tower that stands against the enemy's face, and shelters from it. The glossary's *a fácie* row gives *diante de* where *da face de* is not Portuguese (Ps 37:4, 37:6), and 43:17 *a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis* is *diante do inimigo e do que me persegue* — the same words, so the same wording (rule 6). DRB 'against the face of the enemy'; MS1932 *contra o inimigo*. As the Preces response it must read alone: *Diante do inimigo.* **v2:** the Latinist (minor) wants the face and the sense 'against': *contra a face do inimigo*. Refused: 43:17 has the same three words as *diante do inimigo* and rule 6 asks one wording; the glossary row gives *diante de* for ἀπὸ προσώπου where *da face de* is not Portuguese; and *diante de* holds both the facing and the shelter. His wording is added as an option.

decisions.why: *velaméntum* is a covering or veil (L&S); here and at 62:8b only (grep). Its Greek is σκέπη, the same word as behind *tegmen* at 35:8 (*in tégmine alárum tuárum* → *ao abrigo das vossas asas*), and by D15's test (one Greek word, no difference of sense) the two may share *abrigo*. The glossary's *tegmen* row already refuses *sob a cobertura* (heard as a roof, an insurance, an icing) and keeps *sombra* for *umbra* (16:8b). *Sob o véu* keeps *velaméntum*'s own image, but a veil of wings is a strange picture. Cost: *protegido ao abrigo* sounds a little doubled; the Greek doubles it itself (σκεπασθήσομαι ἐν σκέπῃ). **v2:** the Latinist (minor) asks *sob o véu das vossas asas* for the concrete covering. Refused: the Greek is σκέπη, as 35:8's *tegmen*, and one Greek word with no difference of sense gets one Portuguese word (D15); *sob o véu* was already option 3. No other reader remarked.

decisions.why: ἡμέρας ἐφ᾿ ἡμέρας: days *upon* the king's days. *sobre* keeps the Latin's preposition and its picture of days heaped on days; MS1932 and DRB say *aos dias* ('add days to the days'), which is the sense in plainer grammar. The verb comes first, as Portuguese orders it; the colon ends on *rei*. *rex* lower case, as the DO Latin prints it. **v2:** the stylist: *acrescentar sobre* is not idiomatic — one adds *a* something — and the reciter stumbles. decisions.latin: annos ejus usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis
decisions.why: The colon has no verb: *annos* is still the object of *adícies*, and the Portuguese keeps the ellipsis. The phrase is the only *in diem generatiónis et generatiónis* in the psalter (grep); elsewhere *in generatiónem et generatiónem* is the glossary formula *de geração em geração*. *Até o dia de geração em geração* keeps *usque*, *diem* and the formula; *de geração e geração* is the letter, but not a Portuguese phrase; MS1932 and DRB drop *diem* (*de geração em geração*; 'even to generation and generation'). The sense — a reign without end — is carried by all three. **v2:** both the Latinist (minor) and the stylist refused the hybrid: *de geração em geração* is a fixed idiom of succession, and hung on *o dia* it makes nonsense; the blind reader found *até o dia* hard to parse. Both asked for the letter, *de geração e geração*. Taken — it keeps the Latin's genitive pair and *et*, and the doubling of the noun says 'every generation' without borrowing the idiom. The stylist's added *e* before *os seus anos* is refused: the Latin has no *et*, and the ellipsis is the Latin's.

decisions.why: ἐκζητήσει, 'seek out'. The Latin question can mean 'who shall search it out?' choices.60:2: Rule 6: the opening is 54:2's (*Exáudi, Deus, … → Escutai, Deus, …*), where 53:4 *Deus, exáudi* keeps its own order (*Deus, escutai*). *exaudíre → escutar* (D3), *inténdere → atender* with *a* (D3; 5:3, 16:1a *atendei à minha prece*), *deprecátio → prece* (D35). The two nouns change places against 16:1a because the Latin's do.
choices.60:3: *fines terræ → os confins da terra* (glossary; 21:28, 47:11). *ad te clamávi → a vós clamei*, the Latin's order, so the colon ends on the oxytone *clamei*. *In petra exaltásti me* copies 26:6 *Sobre uma rocha me exaltou* (the *petra* row asks for it), indefinite as the Latin. checks: the second colon is +8 by the counter (which does not elide *-ção se‿an-*, *o‿meu*, *ro-cha‿me*); it carries four Latin members (*dum anxiarétur · cor meum · in petra · exaltásti me*) and none can go; *numa rocha* would save a syllable at the cost of 26:6's wording — accepted. The Latin verse division is DO's, not DRB's (which ends v3 with 'Thou hast conducted me').
choices.60:4: *dedúcere → guiar* (D22; this verse is one of the row's places). *factus es → vos fizestes* (the *fíeri* row, *fazer-se*; 117:21, 117:28b). *quia → porque*. The Tract of 01-31 begins *Factus es spes mea, Dómine*.
choices.60:5: The colon is one of the two places of *velaméntum* (with 62:8b, where Ps 62 should copy *ao abrigo das vossas asas*). The blind reader heard *tenda* as a camping tent as well as God's dwelling — the cost the *tabernáculum* row already records.
choices.60:6: *Deus meus* vocative → *meu Deus*, as in every finished psalm (7:2, 21:3, 34:24). *tu* explicit → *vós*. *exaudísti → escutastes* (D3).
choices.60:7: *regis* → *do rei*, lower case as the DO Latin. *annos ejus → os seus anos* — *seus* is the king's here and cannot mislead.
choices.60:9: *psalmum dícere → entoar um salmo* (17:50, 26:6b; D25's family); the blind reader listed *entoarei* as a word he did not know — the D25 cost, noted, the settled verb kept. *in sǽculum sǽculi → pelos séculos dos séculos* (D27), moved to the head of the verse in v2 (decision `v9order`) so the mediant is not a proparoxytone. checks: the first colon is still long, the formula being eight syllables for five.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (no Diurnal text for this psalm in the parallels file). Liturgical uses found by grep in content/do: the Tract of 01-31 (60:4b–6), the All Saints antiphon (11-01, adapted from 60:4–6), the Prime Preces (60:4b as *Esto nobis, Dómine, turris fortitúdinis. R. A fácie inimíci*; 60:9 as V/R), the Pent02-5 antiphon *Dum anxiarétur * Cor meum*. Hard readings: 60:7 *usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis* (hapax phrase), 60:8 *quis requíret* (open between fathoming and seeking) and the owner of *ejus*, 60:5 *velaméntum* (hapax outside 62:8b; the Greek is 35:8's σκέπη).

Hard checks pass. Soft: 60:3b +8 and 60:9a +7 (accepted, reasons in choices); 60:2a −4, 60:4a +4, 60:5a −3, 60:6a −4, 60:7b −5 within reach of the Latin once elisions are counted. 60:9a closes on a proparoxytone, as the Latin (the settled formula). No cadence rhyme found.
3 minor, no major. 60:7 taken; 60:4 and 60:5 refused (glossary consistency), each kept as an option.
